title: The prompt-diagnosis message carries the pane tail, like the blocked message does
action: Two small repairs, both leftovers the sweep missed. (1) hps-7's `diagnosis_message` quotes only the ONE matched line. `blocked_message`, right above it, quotes its match AND appends a `pane tail:` block. On the case that motivated the whole diagnosis pass — an eight-column clipped pane — the matched line is the arrow-key nav footer, so the message reads `shows what looks like an unanswered prompt: "↑/↓ Na"` and the reader still cannot see the question was a workspace-trust dialog. Give `diagnosis_message` the same pane tail, reusing the helper `blocked_message` already uses rather than writing a second one, so both give-up messages have one shape. Keep the matched line, pane id, job id and remedy sentence exactly as they are; the tail is added, nothing removed. Update the hps-7 assertions on that message text and add one case proving a clipped narrow-pane capture's tail reaches the message. (2) `.bee/config-sample.json`'s `herding` note still teaches two retired rules in its OPERATIONAL RULES sentence: that the pointer is `resent until the pane text echoes it (30 attempts ~1s; herdr's ready flags fire before some agents accept input)` — pane-text echo AND the 30-resend loop are both gone — and that `an agent that stops to ask permission mid-run stalls until the idle-timeout`, which hps-7's diagnosis pass now names instead of silently burning. Rewrite just that sentence pair to the shipped shape: the pointer is submitted once through herdr's own observed submit, the receipt is the worker's ack file (or the round result), a resend fires only when the agent returns to ready with no ack, and a pane sitting on a question is named in the give-up message. Change nothing else in the sample.

The config sample no longer teaches pane-text echo, the 30-resend loop, or a silent permission stall
